rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil glosses praise of God as gratitude or thanks to God.
rows.anchor: يعني الشكر لله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord of the worlds means jinn and humans, as in the description of the Qur'an as a warning to all worlds.
rows.anchor: يعنى الجن والإنس، مثل قوله: ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm are two closely related names, one more delicate than the other; al-Raḥmān means merciful and al-Raḥīm means compassionate through mercy.
rows.anchor: اسمان رفيقان، أحدهما أرق من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Master of the Day of Judgment means the Day of Reckoning, as the verse about being brought to account also says.
rows.anchor: يعنى يوم الحساب، كقوله سبحانه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earthly kings rule in this world, but on Resurrection Day no one owns anything except God, as the Qur'an says dominion belongs to God that day.
rows.anchor: ملوك الدنيا يملكون فى الدنيا، فأخبر سبحانه أنه لا يملك يوم القيامة أحد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To worship God alone means to affirm His oneness, as the feminine participle in another verse means monotheists.
rows.anchor: يعنى نوحد، كقوله سبحانه في المفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant asks God for help in carrying out worship.
rows.anchor: على عبادتك، { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is Islam, since no religion besides Islam is straight.
rows.anchor: يعنى دين الإسلام؛ لأن غير دين الإسلام ليس بمستقيم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading replaces the request to guide with the wording meaning direct or guide us.
rows.anchor: وفى قراءة ابن مسعود: ارشدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those granted favor are the prophets, whom God favored with prophethood.
rows.anchor: يعنى النبيين الذين أنعم الله عليهم بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people under divine anger are the Jews, whom God turned into apes and pigs; the requested path is other than their religion.
rows.anchor: غير اليهود الذين غضب الله عليهم، فجعل منهم القردة والخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straying people are the polytheists, identified here as the Christians.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولا دين المشركين، يعنى النصارى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet related that God divided this sūra between Himself and the servant: praise is thanks, the two mercy names are praise, the King verse is glorification, and the rest belongs to the servant; seeking help is God's special acknowledgment of the servant's plea.
rows.anchor: عن أبى هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil instructs a reader who reaches the closing words to say Āmīn; angels say it too, and if people's response coincides, the group's prior sins are forgiven.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل، قال إذا قرأ أحدكم هذه السورة فبلغ خاتمتها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reports that Satan shrieked when the Opening of the Book was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: لما نزلت فاتحة الكتاب رن إبليس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī identifies the seven oft-repeated verses as the Opening of the Book.
rows.anchor: عن السدى، عن عبد خير، عن على، رضى الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the Prophet's task easier by replacing a verse with one easier than it.
rows.anchor: ونبدلك مكان آية بأيسر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to remind Muhammad means to remind people through the testimony that there is no god but God; the reminder is that testimony.
rows.anchor: يا محمد: اذكر بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever fears God will remember and affirm His oneness; God forgives that person and does not take him to account.
rows.anchor: سيوحد الله من يخشاه، يقول: من يخشاه غفر له، ولم يؤاخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched person treats monotheism lightly or neglects it.
rows.anchor: يقول: ويتهاون بها، يعني بالتوحيد الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one already known by God's prior knowledge as wretched enters the Great Fire, which is Hell.
rows.anchor: قد سبق علم الله فيه بالشقاء الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned neither die to rest nor enjoy a good life; death reaches them everywhere, they burn repeatedly and are restored to punishment, with fire as clothing and food from their own flesh, and they never receive mercy, satiety, or relief.
rows.anchor: لا يموت في النار فيستريح، ولا يحيا حياة طيبة، ولكنه في بلاء ما دام في النار يأتيه الموت من كل مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful person pays alms, bears witness that there is no god but God, and performs the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: قد أفلح من أدى الزكاة، وشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وصلى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People choose the life of this world over the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: بل تختارون الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter is better and more enduring than worldly life.
rows.anchor: والآخرة خير وأبقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The teaching is found in the earlier scriptures: Ibrahim's scrolls and the books of Moses, meaning the Torah; Ibrahim's scrolls have since been taken away.
rows.anchor: يقول: الكتب الأولى { صحف إبراهيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether the account of the Overwhelming has reached the Prophet means that it has; every Qur'anic occurrence of Has it come to you means it has come.
rows.anchor: يعني قد أتاك حديث أهل النار من قوله: تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces are humbled and abased.
rows.anchor: يعني ذليلة { عاملة ناصبة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They labor in the Fire: it consumes them while they eat from it, worn down and humiliated by punishment.
rows.anchor: عاملة في النار، النار تأكله، ويأكل من النار، يعني ناصبة للعذاب صاغرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring is at its ultimate heat. Hell has been heated since its creation; the spring issues from a mountain's base after a seventy-year journey, with black, thick, murky water full of tiny creatures. A fiery iron vessel burns drinkers' cheeks and teeth, then their heart and belly boil and dissolve like lead.
rows.anchor: وهي عين تخرج من أصل جبل طولها مسيرة سبعين عاما، ماؤها أسود كدردي الزيت، كدر غليظ كثير الدعاميص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḍarīʿ is a thorny Meccan tree that animals avoid; Quraysh call its fresh spring growth shibriq, which camels eat while green but avoid when dry. Every harmful land creature has a fiery counterpart appointed over the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: وهي شجرة تكون بمكة كثيرة الشوك لا تقربها دابة في الأرض من شوكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are fed for punishment, not to relieve hunger, so the food neither fattens nor satisfies.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لا يطعمون من أجل الجوع، وإنما من أجل العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed faces are joyful, like the faces of people whose spirits brighten when they get a drink; happiness gathers in their hearts and faces.
rows.anchor: يعني فرحة شبه الله عز وجل وجوههم بوجوه قوم فرحين، إذا أصابوا الشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed person is satisfied with her effort because God approves the work and rewards her for it.
rows.anchor: يعني قد رضي الله عمله، فأثابه الله عز وجل ذلك بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden is called high because Hell lies below it; Hell has descending levels while Paradise has ascending ranks.
rows.anchor: سماها عالية لأن جهنم أسفل منها، وهي دركات، والجنة درجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no idle speech among the people of the Garden: no backbiting, lying, or abuse.
rows.anchor: لا يسمع بعضهم من بعض غيبة، ولا كذب، ولا شتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flowing spring means that rivers run through the Garden.
rows.anchor: في الجنة لأنها فيها تجرى الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised couches are woven with pearl and gold rods and bear seventy mattresses, each as large as a room in this world.
rows.anchor: منسوجة بقضبان الدر والذهب عليها سبعون فراشا، كل فراش قدر غرفة من غرف الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cups are arranged silver vessels, clear like glass, round at the top, and without handles or spouts.
rows.anchor: وهي أكواب من فضة، وهي من الصفاء مثل القوارير مدورة الرءوس ليس لها عرى ولا خراطيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lined cushions are large pillows set in rows on carpets; the word is particular to Quraysh speech.
rows.anchor: يعني الوسائد الكبار العظام مصفوفة على الطنافس، وهي بلغة قريش خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The carpets are spread over one another; God recalls His craftsmanship to make people strive for the Garden and fear the Fire, whose punishment and honor reflect His power.
rows.anchor: يعني طنافس مبسوطة بعضها على بعض، يذكرهم الله عز وجل صنعه ليعتبر عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels are singled out because Arabs had not seen elephants; had the verse mentioned elephants, they would not have marveled at them.
rows.anchor: لأن العرب لم يكونوا رأوا الفيل، وإنما ذكر لهم ما أبصروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is raised five hundred years above the people.
rows.anchor: من فوقهم خمس مائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains are set as pegs in the earth so it will not shift with its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: على الأرض أوتادا لئلا تزول بأهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is spread flat beneath the Kaaba for a distance of five hundred years.
rows.anchor: كيف بسطت من تحت الكعبة مسيرة خمس مائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to warn Mecca's people, like earlier prophets, and has no authority as a king over them.
rows.anchor: أهل مكة يا محمد { إنمآ أنت مذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command that Muhammad is not their master was later abrogated by the sword verse in Sūrat Barāʾa.
rows.anchor: لست عليهم بملك، ثم نسختها آية السيف في براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who turn away and disbelieve are punished in the Hereafter; the punishment is called greater because Hell exceeds the worldly killing and hunger God had threatened.
rows.anchor: يعني أعرض { وكفر } [آية: 23] بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return means their coming back to God, and their reckoning or recompense is easy for Him.
rows.anchor: يعني مصيرهم { ثم إن علينا حسابهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors, continuing the reference to ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, committed sins in the lands.
rows.anchor: يعني الذين عملوا فيها بالمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their spreading corruption means that they multiplied acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأكثروا فيها المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lash of punishment is God's vengeance, which came after their many sins.
rows.anchor: يعني نقمته وكانت نقمته عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is on the lookout along the path: Hell has seven bridges, each a seventy-year journey, guarded by fiery-faced, lightning-eyed angels with whips, hooks, and grappling irons. They question people in sequence about faith, five prayers, alms, Ramadan fasting, pilgrimage, ʿumra, and wrongs against others.
rows.anchor: يعني بالصراط، وذلك أن جهنم عليها سبع قناطر، كل قنطرة مسيرة سبعين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf and ʿAbd Allāh b. Nufayl: after Nufayl advised him to do good and avoid evil, Umayya cited 47:11, asked why God enriched him but impoverished Nufayl, then claimed wealth proved his honor; Ibn Khaṭal said God might indeed have done so.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في أمية بن خلف الجمحي، وعبدالله بن نفيل، أتاه يأمره بالمعروف، وينهاه عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth does not show God's honor or poverty His contempt: God meant to give the rich man ease in this life and make the poor man's reckoning lighter in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: كلا ما أغنيت هذا الغنى لكرامته، ولا أفقرت هذا الفقير لهوانه علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated promise that with hardship comes ease means every difficulty is followed by relief, and every ease by later difficulty.
rows.anchor: ليس من شدة إلا بعدها رخاء، ولا رخاء إلا بعده شدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a break in the discourse, Muqātil resumes the criticism of Umayya: people fail to honor orphans or urge feeding the poor because they do not expect the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ثم انقطع الكلام، ثم ذكر أمية بن خلف الجمحي، وذكر مساوئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating the inheritance greedily means consuming it intensely.
rows.anchor: يعني تأكلون الميراث أكلا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means gathering abundant wealth, and it is an expression in the dialect of Mālik b. Kināna.
rows.anchor: ويجمعون المال جمعا كثيرا، وهي بلغة مالك بن كنانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated crushing means the earth is flattened until the mountains are level with it.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا تركت فاستوت الجبال مع الأرض الممدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the coming of God and the angels, heaven and earth split, and the angels of each heaven descend and stand in separate ranks before God comes.
rows.anchor: تنشق السماوات والأرض، فتنزل ملائكة كل سماء، وتقوم ملائكة كل سماء على حدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul is one reassured by faith.
rows.anchor: يعني المطمئنة بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul returns satisfied with its deeds and approved because of the goodness and recompense God grants it.
rows.anchor: لعملك { مرضية } [آية: 28] بما أعطاك الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering among God's servants means entering His mercy, and entering the Garden is entering it through that mercy.
rows.anchor: يعني في رحمتى { وادخلي } من رحمتي في { جنتي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording parallels Solomon's prayer to be admitted by mercy among God's righteous servants.
rows.anchor: نظيرها في طس النمل، قول سليمان بن داود، عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about Ḥabīb b. ʿAdī, whom Meccans crucified facing Medina. He prayed that if God had good for him, He would turn him toward its qibla; God turned him without human help, and none could turn him back.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في حبيب بن عدي الذي صلبه أهل مكة، وجعلوا وجهه نحو المدينة

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās attributes to the Prophet a description of seven heavens made respectively of water, iron, silver, brass, gold, red ruby, and light; angels of light stand in ranks on the seventh.
rows.anchor: عن عبدالله بن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the she-camel was killed, her calf fled up a mountain and cried three times that its mother had been killed; the people asked Ṣāliḥ what to do, but the calf escaped when they tried to seize it.
rows.anchor: لما عقروا الناقة ابتعد الفصيل حتى صعد على جبل فصاح ثلاث مرات: يا صالح، قتلت أمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ said the three cries gave the people three days: their faces would turn yellow, then red, then black, before punishment on the fourth. They prepared graves, embalmed themselves, and at first mistook the delay for mercy.
rows.anchor: تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك الوعد الذي صاح الفصيل غير مكذوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the fourth day Gabriel blocked the sunlight; people fled back to their graves, and Gabriel's cry caused their souls to leave their bodies while their houses collapsed onto their graves, leaving the town as if it had never existed.
rows.anchor: فصاح بهم جبريل صيحة أن قوموا عليكم لعنة الله، فسالت أرواحهم من أجسادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To have God bring down the destruction for their sin and level it means their houses were leveled onto their graves.
rows.anchor: يعني فسوى بيوتهم على قبورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel's killer did not fear the consequence from God; the passage also recalls the one who rose to kill the camel.
rows.anchor: عاقر الناقة من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine troublemakers included Qudār b. Qadīra, Sālif, Jadʿ, Qayl, Juzayl, Hudhayl, Jamāl b. Mālik, Ḥabāba b. Adhdhādh, and Jamīl b. Jawād; this is linked to the nine corrupt people of the city.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان أصحاب الشراب تسعة نفر منهم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says some names in this list agree with the camel killers named in Sūrat al-Naml, while the rest may be another group's names; God knows best.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح: بعض هؤلاء المسمين يوافق تسمية عاقري الناقة في سورة النمل

rows.speaker: جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Gabriel glosses finding Muhammad astray as his being without guidance, then God guided him to His religion; the Prophet responds that his Lord showed him favor and is worthy of praise, and repeats the response when told God found him poor and enriched him.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل، عليه السلام: { ووجدك ضآلا } على الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke or scowl at an orphan, since Muhammad himself had been an orphan.
rows.anchor: لا تنهره، ولا تعبس في وجهه، فقد كنت يتيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke a poor petitioner when he asks, since Muhammad had once been poor.
rows.anchor: لا تنهره إذا سألك فقد كنت فقيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To speak of the Lord's favor means to thank God for the blessings named in the sūra and tell how He changed the Prophet's condition for the better.
rows.anchor: يعني اشكر الله على ما ذكر في هذه السورة، وما صنع الله عز وجل بك من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil says Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā, Sūrat al-Layl, and Sūrat Alam Nashraḥ were revealed in Mecca together; Muhammad shared their message privately with trusted people.
rows.anchor: أنزلت هاتين السورتين جميعا بمكة: والضحى، والليل، وألم نشرح لك صدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel demonstrated ritual washing and prayer at upper Mecca by striking the ground until a spring burst forth; Muhammad washed, prayed behind him, then told Khadīja, who also prayed with him.
rows.anchor: فدفع الأرض بيديه فانفجرت عين ماء، فتوضأ جبريل، عليه السلام، ليرى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وضوء الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the Prophet's breast means expanding it after it had been constricted and faith had not entered until God guided him; this recalls 93:7 and 42:52.
rows.anchor: ألم نوسع لك صدرك بعد ما كان ضيقا لا يلح فيه الإيمان حتى هداه الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four hundred Muslim Companions of the Bench lived in the Prophet's mosque without a Medina clan, shared donated food with the poor, and went to fight Banū Sulaym; seventy were killed, grieving the Prophet and Muslims.
rows.anchor: أربع مائة رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أصحاب الصفة، كانوا قوما مسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the seventy were killed, the Prophet prayed against the enemy in the dawn prayer's qunūt, asking God to destroy them; God said the Prophet had no say over the matter and might forgive or punish them.
rows.anchor: كان يدعو عليهم في دبر كل صلاة الغداة يقنت فيها، ويدعو عليهم أن يهلكهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's delay of punishment reflected prior knowledge that those people would accept Islam; the expanded breast means expansion through faith and monotheism until the Prophet could declare there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: في تأخير العذاب عنهم، لعلم قد سبق فيهم أن يسلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about denying judgment addresses ʿAdī b. Rabīʿa: after beauty and youth give way to old age, the One who changed him can resurrect and hold him to account.
rows.anchor: يعني عدي بين ربيعة بالدين، يعني بالبعث بعد الصورة الحسنة والشباب، بعد الهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the wisest judge who will decide between Muhammad and Mecca's deniers; the Prophet answers that He is the best separator, and every Qur'anic question beginning Is not God means I am God.
rows.anchor: على أن يحكم بينك وبين أهل مكة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن أبي عبيدة
rows.claim: Anas reports from Abū ʿUbayda that every gray hair on a person who grew old in Islam earns a good deed and becomes light on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، عن أنس بن مالك، قال: من شاب رأسه في الإسلام، ولحيته كانت له بكل شعرة حسنة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas attributes to the Prophet an account of life stages: before puberty a child's good deeds go to the parents and sins to neither; after puberty angels record deeds, while ages forty through ninety bring successive protections, lighter reckoning, repentance, heavenly affection, forgiveness, and household intercession; in decrepit age former good deeds are still credited and new sins are not.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read in the name of your Lord means in the name of the One; the One who created refers to the human being.
rows.anchor: اقرأ باسم ربك } يعني بالواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first revelation consisted of the first five verses of this sūra. An ʿalaq is a drop that remains twenty nights before turning to water and then blood.
rows.anchor: وكان أول شىء نزل من القرآن خمس آيات من أول هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen passage means God taught writing and taught the human being the Qur'an, knowledge previously unknown.
rows.anchor: الكتابة { بالقلم علم الإنسان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil relates that Abū Jahl adorned his idol Hubal with a gold necklace and musk, thanking it for a year with a thousand camel births and a Syrian caravan profit of ten thousand gold mithqāls; Hubal stood eighteen cubits high inside the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: فإذا أبو جهل يقلد إلهه الذى يعبده طوقا من ذهب، وقد طيبه بالمسك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet rebukes Abū Jahl for thanking an idol for gifts from God, invites him to worship the one God who created and provided for him and his forefathers, and promises this life and the next if he follows.
rows.anchor: أعطاك إلهك وشكرت غيره، أما والله لله فيك نقمة، فانظر متى تكون

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abū Jahl threatens to strike the Prophet's forelock or throw him face-first if he finds him at the sanctuary worshipping other gods, swears by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and asks whether these are God's daughters; Muhammad denies God has a child.
rows.anchor: واللات والعزى رب هذه البنية لئن لم تنته عن مقالتك هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation of God teaching the human what he did not know came while the Prophet was at al-Arāk in the forenoon.
rows.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يومئذ بالأراك ضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person rebels against God's favors when he sees himself as self-sufficient; this specifically describes wealthy Abū Jahl's arrogance in clothes, transport, food, and drink, and the warning that he will return to God means resurrection.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا أصاب مالا أشر يعني بطر في ثيابه، وفى مراكبه، وفى طعامه وشرابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat of return to God warns Abū Jahl about the Resurrection; the forelock threat later names him, and the following verse calls that forelock lying and sinful.
rows.anchor: فخوفه الله الرجعة إليه، فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When prayer was prescribed for Muhammad in Mecca, Abū Jahl threatened to cut off his head if he saw him praying; the verse's man who forbids a servant from prayer is the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فرضت عليه الصلاة بمكة، فقال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلى لأضربن عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person in the question is Muhammad, and being commanded to piety means being commanded to sincerity.
rows.anchor: يعني محمدا { على الهدى } [آية: 11] { أو أمر بالتقوى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier who turns away is Abū Jahl, who rejects the Qur'an; God sees both the Prophet alone and Abū Jahl's assembled company.
rows.anchor: يعني وأعرض { ألم يعلم } أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abū Jahl does not stop his denial and turning away from Muhammad, God will seize his forelock forcefully; angels drag him face-first into the Fire for his sin, since the forelock is described as lying and sinful.
rows.anchor: لنأخذن بالناصية أخذا شديدا، ثم أخبر عنه أنه فاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jahl's supporters and gathering are Banū Makhzūm.
rows.anchor: يعني بني مخزوم، يعني ناصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zabāniya are more fiercely angry at Abū Jahl than Banū Makhzūm are at Muhammad; a Prophetic report pictures Abū Jahl dragged face-first over embers in Hell, regretting that he mistreated Muhammad and begging to return and make his clan believe.
rows.anchor: فهم أشد غضبا عليه من بني مخزوم على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not obey the prohibition on prayer, but must prostrate and draw near. Polytheists began with prostration, then bowed, stood, and asked idols; God later changed the Prophet's order to standing, bowing, then prostrating.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يبدؤون بالسجود، ثم بعد السجود بالركوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering means a supporter, and the zabāniya are the keepers of Hell, with their feet in the lowest earth and heads in the sky.
rows.anchor: يعني خزنة جهنم أرجلهم في الأرضين السفلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to obey Abū Jahl by abandoning prayer; prostration means prayer to God and drawing near means obeying Him.
rows.anchor: يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تطع أبا جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing the mention of the zabāniya, Abū Jahl turned away although he had been about to attack Muhammad; when asked whether he feared them, he said he did.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع أبو جهل ذكر الزبانية، قال: قد جاء وعد الله وانصرف عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an came down from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven and its angelic scribes; each year's revelation descended on the Night of Decree according to what Gabriel would convey to the Prophet through the following year, until the Qur'an had all descended from heaven.
rows.anchor: أنزله الله عز وجل من اللوح المحفوظ إلى سماء الدنيا، إلى السفرة، وهم الكتبة من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night of Decree is in the month of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: من شهر رمضان من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question What will make you know the Night of Decree magnifies its importance.
rows.anchor: تعظيما لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship on that night is better than worship in a thousand months that contain no Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: العمل فيها خير من العمل في ألف شهر فيما سواها ليس فيها ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels and the Spirit descend at sunset by God's command, carrying mercy and everything decreed for that year through the next year.
rows.anchor: في تلك الليلة عند غروب الشمس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the Spirit as an enormous human-shaped angel who stands in a rank with the angels; the report connects this figure to the question about the Spirit.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: الروح على صورة إنسان عظيم الخلقة، وهو الذي قال الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is peace, blessing, and goodness until dawn rises.
rows.anchor: هى سلام وبركة وخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book means Jews and Christians, the polytheists are Arab idolaters, and remaining apart means ceasing from disbelief and polytheism; the clear proof is Muhammad, who explains their error.
rows.anchor: { منفكين } يعني منتهين عن الكفر والشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book asked when the messenger they found described in their scripture would be raised, while the Arabs said they would be sincere worshippers if they had a reminder from earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: أهل الكتاب قالوا: متى يبعث الذي نجده في كتابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purified pages are the Book recited by Muhammad, called pages because it contains many kinds of qualities and is free of disbelief and polytheism; anything written can be called pages.
rows.anchor: يعني يقرأ صحفا مطهرة، يعني كتابا لأنها جماعة فيها خصال كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upright writings are a straight book of truth without crookedness or disagreement; it is plural because the Qur'an contains many different subjects.
rows.anchor: يعني كتابا مستقيما على الحق ليس فيه عوج، ولا اختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews and Christians divided over Muhammad only after the proof came: before his mission they agreed in affirming him because his description was in their books, but they split when God sent him from outside Isaac's descendants.
rows.anchor: لم يزل الذين كفروا مجتمعين على تصديق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، حتى بعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some People of the Book accepted Muhammad, including ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām and Torah followers, and forty Gospel followers including Buḥayrā; the rest of the People of the Book rejected him.
rows.anchor: عبدالله بن سلام وأصحابه من أهل التوراة، ومن أهل الإنجيل أربعون رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad commanded them to worship God alone, with sincere monotheism, as Muslims rather than polytheists, to perform the five obligatory prayers and pay the obligatory alms; this is the upright religion.
rows.anchor: يعني به التوحيد { حنفآء } يعني مسلمين غير مشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists remain in Hell and do not die there.
rows.anchor: يقول: يقيمون فيها لا يموتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are the worst creatures among the people of the earth.
rows.anchor: يعني شر الخليقة من أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good are the best creatures among people of the earth.
rows.anchor: يعني خير الخليقة من أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is recompense in the afterlife: Gardens of Eden, where they never die; God is pleased with them for obedience and they are pleased with His reward, provided they feared Him in this world.
rows.anchor: لا يموتون { رضى الله عنهم } بالطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term al-bariyya can designate every creature made from earth.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء خلق من التراب فإنه يسمى البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection, the earth is shaken by the force of Isrāfīl's blast; it cracks and breaks what is on it, then cannot rest until it casts out its mountains, buildings, and trees, which return inside it.
rows.anchor: تزلزت يوم القيامة من شدة صوت إسرافيل، عليه السلام، يعني تحركت، فتفطرت حتى تكسر كل شىء عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth brings out people, animals, jinn, and devils from within; it becomes empty and is spread anew as a shining white land like silver or wool, untouched by sin or bloodshed.
rows.anchor: وأخرجت ما في جوفها من الناس والدواب، والجن، وما عليها من الشياطين، فصارت خالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the first trumpet blast all creatures die; a call from beneath the Throne above the seventh heaven announces it, then at the second blast Isrāfīl calls from the rock of Jerusalem for the dead to come out for judgment on the new land called al-Sāhira.
rows.anchor: فأما الأولى فينادى من تحت العرش من فوق السماء السابعة، وأما الأخرى فمن بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's burdens also include the dead and the wealth stored inside it.
rows.anchor: أخرجت ما فيها من الموتى والأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human asking what is wrong with the earth is the disbeliever panicking because the ground speaks about what was done on it.
rows.anchor: قال الكافر جزعا ما لها تنطق بما عمل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth reports good deeds such as affirming God's oneness, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, ʿumra, jihad, and obedience, rejoicing the believer; it lists idolatry, adultery, theft, wine-drinking, and other sins to rebuke the disbeliever.
rows.anchor: تقول الأرض وحد الله على ظهري، وصلى علي، وصام، وحج، واعتمر، وجاهد، وأطاع ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limbs and guardian angels also testify against people, intensifying their shame despite God's prior knowledge; the disbeliever asks why the earth speaks.
rows.anchor: وتشهد عليه أيضا الجوارح، والحفظة من الملائكة، مع علم الله عز وجل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recording angel who accompanied a person in this life explains that the earth has testified against its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: قال الملك الذي كان موكلا به في الدنيا يكتب حسناته وسيئاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires the earth to speak and report its deeds.
rows.anchor: يوحى الله إليها بأن تحدث أخبارها، وأيضا أن ربك أوحى لها بالكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the gathering and reckoning, people depart in separate groups for their homes in Paradise or Hell, never to meet again; the same separation is described elsewhere.
rows.anchor: يرجع الناس من بعد العرض والحساب إلى منازلهم من الجنة والنار متفرقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are divided into two groups, one for Paradise and one for the Fire; seeing their works means seeing good and evil deeds directly.
rows.anchor: يقول: انتصف الناس فريقين والأشتات الذين لا يلتقون أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speck's weight is the weight of the tiniest red ant, scarcely visible; people see such good and evil deeds in their record on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: يعني وزن نملة أصغر النمل الأحمر التي لا تكاد نراها من صغرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs dismissed small charity and minor sins, so God encourages even a little charity and warns that small wrongdoing can grow; the teaching was revealed about two men in Medina.
rows.anchor: فزهدهم الله عز وجل في الذنب الحقير، ورغبهم في الصدقة القليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of the two men refused a crust or small piece to a petitioner, saying one is rewarded only for giving beloved food; the Qur'an's description of those who feed from love is cited against him.
rows.anchor: كان أحدهما إذا أتاه السائل يستقل أن يعطيه الكسرة أو النمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other man treated a small lie, glance, or backbiting as insignificant, assuming only major sinners were promised Hell; a minor sin appears like mountains at judgment, while worldly good deeds seem smaller than one good deed.
rows.anchor: وكان الآخر يتهاون بالذنب اليسير الكذبة، والنظرة، والغيبة، وأشباه ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abū Rawq explains that the Lord's word is fulfilled truthfully and justly: those who follow Islam's ordinances receive Paradise, while deniers receive the just recompense of Hell.
rows.anchor: لمن جاء بشرائع الإسلام، فله الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil lists the Prophet's Companions buried in Basra as ʿImrān b. Ḥuṣayn, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Zayd b. Ṣawḥān, and Anas b. Mālik, and lists Qur'an memorizers as Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, Muʿādh, Ubayy b. Kaʿb, Zayd b. Thābit, and Abū Zayd.
rows.anchor: أسماء من دفن بالبصرة من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ورحمة الله عليهم، عمران بن حصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil gives genealogical notes: Shuʿayb is from Midian and Abraham; David's lineage runs through Judah and Jacob; Isaac is Abraham's son; Hūd is ʿĀbir; Ṣāliḥ descends from Arfakhshadh and Noah; Abraham is called Ibrākhīm and father of nations in the Gospel; Lot is Abraham's nephew, and Sarah is Lot's sister and Abraham's wife.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم اسمه إبرخيم، وفي الإنجيل أبو الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil says beauty is apportioned in ten shares: five to Eve, three to Sarah, one to Joseph, and one to everyone else.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: الحسن عشرة أجزاء خمسة لحواء، وثلاثة لسارة، وواحد ليوسف

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr says angels asked for Paradise after explaining that they are near to God, bear the Throne, and record deeds; God said He would not make the righteous descendants of the one created by His hands equal to beings made by the command Be, and al-Musayyib linked this to the best of creation.
rows.anchor: عن عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص، قال: قالت الملائكة: نحن المقربون منا حملة العرش

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن سلام
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām says Adam is God's most honored creature; when asked whether Gabriel and Michael outrank him, he says they are carried like the sun and moon, and another report says the one worshipped is more honored than the one prostrating.
rows.anchor: عن عبدالله بن سلام، قال: إن الله عز وجل لم يخلق خلقا أكرم عليه من آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is witness to the human being's disbelief and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: إن الله عز وجل على كفر قرط لشهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good means wealth, and the human being loves wealth intensely.
rows.anchor: يعني المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means, will he not know, when the dead in graves are resurrected?
rows.anchor: يعني بعث { ما في القبور } [آية: 9]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is gathered from breasts is their good and evil, distinguished from one another.
rows.anchor: من الخير والشر، يعني تميز ما في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day God knows which people are righteous and which are wicked.
rows.anchor: بالصالح منهم والطالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about blessings addresses Meccan disbelievers who enjoyed worldly prosperity and will be asked whether they thanked God for it; the same reckoning is cited at 46:20.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار مكة كانوا في الدنيا في الخير والنعمة، فيسألون يوم القيامة عن شكر ما كانوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report about the people of Hell, they beg Mālik for a day or even an hour outside, then ask to return to earth and act differently. Mālik recites the warning about worldly pleasures, asks how they now find Saqar, and refuses death or any respite, leaving them in greater torment.
rows.anchor: إذا جمع الكفار في النار صرخوا: يا مالك، أضجت لحومنا، وأحرقت جلودنا، وجاعت وأعطشت أفواهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being questioned about blessing means being asked whether one thanked God for it; the ungrateful person is the disbeliever who did not find guidance or give thanks.
rows.anchor: يعني الشكر للنعيم الذي أعطاه الله عز جل، فلم يهتد ولم يشكر، يعني الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elephant expedition was led by Abraha al-Ashram and his companions: he sent his son Abū Yaksūm with a large army and an elephant to destroy the Sanctuary, make the elephant a worshipped focus like the Kaaba, and kill anyone who resisted. They stopped at al-Muʿammas just outside the sacred territory.
rows.anchor: يعني أبرهة بن الأشرم اليمانى وأصحابه، وذلك أنه كان بعث أبا يكسوم بن أبرهة اليمانى الحبشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elephant refused to enter Mecca: it knelt when urged toward the city, even after the soldiers gave it wine, and when released it ran back toward where it had come from, so the army withdrew that year.
rows.anchor: فلما أردوا أن يسوقوا الفيل إلى مكة لم يدخل الفيل الحرم، وبرك فأمر أبو يكسوم أن يسقوه الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A year or two later Quraysh traders left a fire burning at a Christian church near the coast; wind spread it into a blaze, and the enraged Najāshī heard the news.
rows.anchor: تركوا النار، كما هي في يوم عاصف، فعجت الريح واضطرم الهيكل نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab rulers near the Najāshī, including Ḥajar b. Shurayḥbīl and Abraha al-Ṣabāḥ al-Kindī, offered to destroy Quraysh's Kaaba and seize its people and property in revenge.
rows.anchor: لا تكاد ولا تغلب، نحن مؤازرون لك على كعبة قريش التي بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Najāshī sent al-Aswad b. Maqṣūd, the farmers' battalions, Arab kings, and the elephant Maḥmūd toward Mecca; they took the marked camels and mares belonging to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: فأخرج كتائبه جماهير معهم الفيل، واسمه محمود، فسار بهم وبمن معه من ملوك العرب تلقاء مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A herdsman galloped to Mecca, climbed Ṣafā, and warned that the army and its elephant were coming to demolish the Kaaba, destroy Quraysh's honor, and plunder their lives and wealth.
rows.anchor: فصعد إلى الصفا فرقى عليه، ثم نادى بصوت رفيع: يا صباحاه، يا صباحاه، أتتكم السودان معها فيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went to the army camp and would not leave without his camels and mares; the commanders mockingly directed him to the Najāshī, who returned the animals.
rows.anchor: واللات والعزى، لا أرجع حتى أرجع معي بخيلي، ولقاحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib offered all his family and wealth to make the Najāshī turn away from the Kaaba, but was refused; he recovered his livestock, while Quraysh fled to the mountains.
rows.anchor: هل لك إلى أن أعطيك أهلي ومالي، وأهل قومي، وأموالهم، ولقاحهم على أن تنصرف عن كعبة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib stayed by the House, trusting his ancestors' teaching that the Kaaba had a Lord who would protect it and that the Christian army would not prevail.
rows.anchor: فقد نبأنى أجدادى أن للكعبة ربا يمنعها، ولن تغلب النصرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind elder Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī advised ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to consecrate his camels to God and release them inside the sanctuary, hoping an enemy attack on them would provoke the Kaaba's Lord to punish the army.
rows.anchor: اعمد إلى ما ترى من إبلك، فاجعلها حرما لله، وقلدها نعالا، ثم أرسلها في حرم الله

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: In verse, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib asks God to protect His sanctuary as a servant protects his property, says the crosses and elephant army cannot defeat God's power, and condemns those who seek glory by violating His sacred place.
rows.anchor: يا رب إن العبد يمنع رحله فأمنع حلالك لا يغلبن صليبهم

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: His prayer names al-Aswad b. Maqṣūd as the taker of the marked herd and asks God to shame him among the mountains, valleys, and sacred sites.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا عليهم فقال: اللهم أخز الأسود بن مقصود، الآخذ الهجمة بعد التقليد

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود
rows.claim: Abū Masʿūd says God protected the sanctuary when the Yemeni king Tubbaʿ sought to destroy it: God afflicted them with three days of darkness, after which Tubbaʿ clothed and honored the Kaaba and sacrificed camels there.
rows.anchor: فقد نزل تبع ملك اليمن بصحن هذا البيت، وأراد هدمه، فمنعه الله عن ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود
rows.claim: Abū Masʿūd sees strange birds approaching from the sea, unlike birds of any Arab region; they are locust-sized, carry stones in their beaks, fly in successive flocks behind a distinctive leader, and rain stones on the army, each reportedly bearing its victim's name.
rows.anchor: وهي طير أبابيل يتبع بعضها بعضا، أمام كل رفقة منها طائر يقودها أحمر المنقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men descend from the mountain and find the army dead; stones penetrate a soldier's helmet into his brain and pierce elephants and other animals until the stones disappear into the ground.
rows.anchor: يقع الحجر في بيضة الرجل فيخرقها، حتى يقع في دماغه، ويخرق الفيل والدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib digs two pits, fills them with red gold and jewels, and invites Abū Masʿūd to choose either or both.
rows.anchor: فحفر حتى عمق في الأرض وملأه من الذهب الأحمر والجوهر الجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Masʿūd lets ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib choose a treasure pit for him; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib gives him the better goods. The people share the remaining wealth, raise ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's standing in Quraysh, and his family prospers.
rows.anchor: فقال عبدالمطلب: إنى لم أجعل أجود المتاع في حفرتى وهي لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God defended the Kaaba and its qibla by sending an army the invaders could not withstand, as He had them in His watch and grip.
rows.anchor: ودفع الله عز وجل عن كعبته وقبلته وسلط عليهم جنودا لا قبل لهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners of the elephant means al-Aswad b. Maqṣūd and the army and Arab kings with him.
rows.anchor: يعني الأسود بن مقصود، ومن معه من الجيش وملوك العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plot was to destroy the Kaaba and plunder its inhabitants; its ending in misguidance means their failure and loss.
rows.anchor: يعني متتابعة كلها تترى بعضها على إثر بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abābīl means successive flocks, following one another in sequence.
rows.anchor: يعني متتابعة كلها تترى بعضها على إثر بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjīl means stones mixed with clay.
rows.anchor: يعني بحجارة خلطها الطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invaders are compared to eaten chaff, meaning decayed crop leaves. The army was destroyed forty years before the Prophet's birth at the edge of the sanctuary and never entered it.
rows.anchor: فشبههم بورق الزرع المأكول يعني البالي، وكان أصحاب الفيل قبل مولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأربعين سنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة بن خالد
rows.claim: Ikrima b. Khālid's poem recalls the army and elephants being held at Mecca and the feared battle, serving as poetic testimony to the expedition's defeat.
rows.anchor: حبست رب الجيش والأفيال وقد رعوا بمكة الأجبال قد خشينا منهم القتال

rows.speaker: صفوان بن أمية المخزومي
rows.claim: Ṣafwān b. Umayya's poem calls on God who protects the Ḥums and sanctuary, praising Him as mighty and as the one who holds the elephant army.
rows.anchor: يا واهب الحى الحلال الأحمس وما لهم من طارق ومنفس أنت العزيز ربنا لا تدنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem continuation describes Kinda rulers around the elephant army as young hawks amid battle; after joining the alliance, they fled.
rows.anchor: حوله من ملوك كندة فتيان ملاويث في الهياج صقور حالفوه ثم انذعروا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding line says every religion will perish on Judgment Day except the upright hanif religion.
rows.anchor: كل دين يوم القيامة عند الله دين الحنيفة بور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh traded in winter toward Jordan and Palestine, whose coast was warmer, then went to Yemen for provisions in summer because the northern route and sea were too hot. God caused Abyssinians to ship food to Mecca, allowing Meccans to buy it a two-day journey away and relieving their repeated travel and provisioning burden.
rows.anchor: كانوا يمتارون في الشتاء من الأردن وفلسطين، لأن ساحل البحر أدفا، فإذا كان الصيف تركوا طريق الشتاء والبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says merchants did not come to Quraysh and could not find their way to them, so Quraysh provisioned their people from Syria in winter and Yemen in summer; Abyssinian ships later brought food to Jeddah, one night's journey away, relieving the burden.
rows.anchor: لا ميرة لقريش، ولا اختلاف، وذلك أن قريشا كانت لا تأتيهم التجار، ولا يهتدون إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil glosses īlāf as provisioning and travel or exchange.
rows.anchor: والإيلاف من المؤنة والاختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh should worship the Lord of this House because He relieved them of food and fear, becoming habituated to His worship as they had become used to commerce with the Abyssinians.
rows.anchor: لأن رب هذا البيت كفاهم مؤنة الخوف والجوع، فليألفوا العبادة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fed them by causing the Abyssinians to ship food and protected them from killing and enslavement, dangers common among the Arabs, by defending the people of the sanctuary from enemies.
rows.anchor: يعني القتل والسبي، وذلك أن العرب في الجاهلية كان يقتل بعضهم بعضا، ويغير بعضهم على بعض
